reading.text:
# Reading: spec ex_brownian_reduction (Example 5.2: "the assumptions and the solution notions at nu = 0 reduce to their Brownian forms")

Example 5.2: remove the Poisson channel (filtration generated by W and F_0, Brownian PRP), delete
the U-coordinate (H reduced to R^n x R^m x R^{m x d}); "merely setting h = 0 on a Brownian-Poisson
basis is not a reduction". "The assumptions reduce to W2-Lipschitz joint-law dependence of
(X,Y,Z) under G-monotonicity, the condition of [BYZ (A1)]". Remark 2.10 identifies nu = 0 with this
Brownian case (fibre L^2(nu) trivial, dU = 0).
The clause realises the reduction at nu = 0. A faithful formal statement must contain, at nu = 0
(so L^2(nu) = {0}, the U-coordinate and every jump term vanish, N = 0 a.s.):
* the ASSUMPTIONS reduce: for coefficients on H at nu = 0 obtained from Brownian coefficients
  (b,sigma,f,g) on R^n x R^m x R^{m x d} and P2 of that space (via the U-forgetting projection),
  Assumption 2.3 (resp. 2.5) holds iff the Brownian Lipschitz condition (resp. the Brownian
  G-monotonicity: the pairing without the jump term, the beta1 block without ||G^T dU||^2) holds;
  W2 on P2(H) equals W2 of the (X,Y,Z)-marginals there;
* the SOLUTION notions reduce: Theta = (X,Y,Z,U) solves (1.1) at nu = 0 iff U = 0 (a.e.) and
  (X,Y,Z) solves the Brownian MV-FBSDE (no Poisson integrals), in the corresponding classes
  (HH vs its Brownian analogue);
* both directions (an equivalence), or at least the forms in which the paper uses them; a statement
  that only records "the jump terms are 0 at nu = 0" without relating the assumption/solution
  predicates to Brownian ones would be narrower.
Setting: arbitrary dims n, m, d, G full rank, the standing basis with nu = 0 (or the Brownian
basis). This is a "reduction" remark; any precise faithful form must be an iff between the
nu = 0 instances of the paper's predicates and their Brownian counterparts.

comparison.text:
# Comparison: ex_brownian_reduction (Example 5.2)

Lean (Sec5BrownianReduction.lean): for every basis with intensity nu = 0 (any countably generated
E, any d, any G0 independent of the driver), all n, m, T and every coefficient system C on
H = R^n x R^m x R^{m x d} x L^2(0; R^m) (the jump channel being {0}), with F^B = enlBrownian (the
usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W and G0, equal to enlJoint at nu = 0):
 (a) forall L: Assumption23 over enlJoint <-> BrownianAssumption23 over F^B (L >= 0, interior
     |db| + |dsigma| + |df| <= L(|dX| + |dY| + |dZ| + W2(projP2 mu, projP2 mu')) with projP2 the
     (X,Y,Z)-marginal in the Hilbert-normed R^n x R^m x R^{m x d}, and (2.6)); and at each t
     LipInteriorAt <-> BrownianLipInteriorAt;
 (b) at each t and for all G, beta1, beta2: Mono27At <-> BrownianMonoAt (the pairing without the
     jump term, the beta1 block without ||G^T dU||^2); Assumption25 <-> BrownianAssumption25 (same
     terminal inequality and admissible constants);
 (c) forall xi0, X, Y, Z, U: Solution (1.1 in HH) <-> (U marked predictable for F^B, vanishing
     off [0,T], zero energy) and BrownianSolution (the forward-backward system without Poisson
     integrals, driven by W over F^B, coefficients along (X_s,Y_s,Z_s,0), in HH); the same for
     WeakSolution <-> ... BrownianWeakSolution (H_weak).

Against my reading:
* Assumptions reduce, as an iff, to W2-Lipschitz dependence on the joint law of (X,Y,Z) and the
  jump-free G-monotonicity: yes ((a), (b)), at the level of Assumptions 2.3, 2.5 and of the
  pointwise-in-time forms.
* Solution notions reduce, as an iff: U = 0 in L^2(dt x dP x nu) (automatic at nu = 0) and
  (X,Y,Z) solves the Brownian system, in HH and in H_weak: yes ((c)).
* Filtration generated by W and F_0: yes (enlBrownian; the hypothesis hind0 makes W Brownian for
  it).
* All dims, all T, all coefficient systems: yes.
Representation choices:
1. The "Brownian coefficients" are the given C on H at nu = 0 (whose U-channel L^2(0) = {0}),
   rather than coefficients on the reduced space R^n x R^m x R^{m x d}; the two are in bijection
   (projB/liftB identify H at nu = 0 with the reduced space, every law on H at nu = 0 is the lift
   of its (X,Y,Z)-marginal), and the Brownian forms read the law through projP2 with the
   Hilbert-norm W2 of the reduced space, as the paper's "W2-Lipschitz joint-law dependence of
   (X,Y,Z)".
2. The reduction is realised inside the model as nu = 0 (as Remark 2.10 does), with the solution
   predicates still carrying a U argument that the iff forces to be the trivial integrand; the
   paper's warning that setting h = 0 on a Brownian-Poisson basis is not a reduction is respected
   because at nu = 0 the Poisson integral and U genuinely vanish.
3. Assumptions 2.2 and 2.4 and (2.3) have no jump terms to delete (h's origin value and Borel
   measurability are trivial in L^2(0)), so they are not restated.
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices, each harmless:
1. The Brownian forms are stated for the same coefficient system C on H at nu = 0, whose jump
   channel L^2(0; R^m) is {0}, rather than for coefficients on R^n x R^m x R^{m x d}; projB/liftB
   identify the two spaces, every law on H at nu = 0 is the lift of its (X,Y,Z)-marginal, and the
   W2 of the Brownian form is that of the (X,Y,Z)-marginals with the Hilbert norm, as printed.
2. "Removing the Poisson channel" is realised as the intensity nu = 0 inside the model (as Remark
   2.10 identifies it); the filtration is enlBrownian, the usual augmentation of the one generated
   by W and F_0, which equals the joint one at nu = 0; the solution predicates keep a U argument
   that the equivalence forces to be the zero integrand.
3. Only Assumptions 2.3 and 2.5 (and the solution notions) are restated, the others having no
   jump terms.
